solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Desert Fox set time to surround men in capital route

indicators.note: the shuffled letters plus T are told to go round the next piece, which sits inside them
set in the sense of fixed into a new arrangement, so the letters of the two words are reshuffled

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Rommel, the Desert Fox, fixes a time for his forces to encircle troops on a road to the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert Fox' looks like Rommel the general, but it is the anagram fodder, with 'set' as the signal; 'to surround' wraps the result round the men. The street is London's main shopping thoroughfare.
explanation.definitionFit: London's famous shopping street is a thoroughfare in the British capital, hence a route in the capital.

clue.text: Bunting taken from door to landing

indicators.note: the answer's letters are lifted out of the run of letters in the next three words

explanation.surface: Bunting decorations removed along the way from the front door to the landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunting' reads as festive flags; here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European songbird belonging to the bunting family, once eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: In tree see female insect

parts.note: the fir is a coniferous tree

indicators.note: the female's letter is placed in the bishop's seat

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, so a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Up a tree you can spot a female insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a noun here: a diocese, and Ely in Cambridgeshire is the classic crossword one.
explanation.definitionFit: A firefly is a beetle that glows at night, so it is a kind of insect.

clue.text: Irrepressible soldiers one found in quiet setting

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

indicators.note: the single letter for one turns up inside the word for quiet
the word for quiet acts as the setting, the surround, holding the letter

parts.note: silent means quiet
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Tough soldiers, one of them discovered in a peaceful place.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone irrepressible bounces back from setbacks, which is the springy toughness of a resilient person.

clue.text: Very high temperature inside for water basin

indicators.note: the abbreviation for temperature goes within the phrase meaning very high

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
up means high, as in 'up in the sky'

explanation.surface: A water basin holding something at a scorching temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very high' looks like a description of the temperature, but it supplies two separate words that 'inside' then opens to take the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoup is a basin for holy water near a church door, or more generally a drinking vessel.

clue.text: Some seaman upset in difficult situation

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: part means some, a portion
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Some sailor, distressed at being stuck in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' reads as a quantifier but is the word PART.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat trap is figuratively a predicament one cannot escape, a trap-like difficult situation.

clue.text: A quote recalled about old times in curious collection

indicators.note: the reversed phrase goes about, around, the letters for old and times
recalled read as called back, so the whole assembly is turned round

parts.note: to cite is to quote
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A quotation remembered about bygone days in an odd anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns A CITE round to ETICA, and 'about' wraps that round XO.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are strange or foreign curiosities, so a collection of curious objects.

clue.text: Provided in turn, in vessels, hot and cold food

indicators.note: in turn means turned round, so the word for provided reads backwards

parts.note: if means provided, as in 'provided that'

indicators.note: the letters for hot and cold go in the word for vessels

parts.note: ships are vessels
H is the tap abbreviation for hot
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: Supplied in sequence, in dishes, both hot and cold food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' suggests dishes in the food surface, but it means boats. FISH AND CHIPS is Britain's classic takeaway of battered fish and fried potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Battered fish with chipped potatoes is a classic British takeaway meal, plainly food.

clue.text: Home birds being those confined

parts.note: in means at home
terns are seabirds

explanation.surface: Pet birds are the ones kept caged.
explanation.definitionFit: Internees are people confined, often during wartime; the noun interns has this older sense of detainees.

clue.text: Exhausted old couple breaking vase

indicators.note: the word for couple breaks into the vase, splitting it

parts.note: an urn is a vase
a couple is two

explanation.surface: A worn-out elderly pair smashing a vase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outworn is used up or spent, the state of being exhausted.

clue.text: Fresh morning mist envelops road in settlement

parts.note: new means fresh

indicators.note: the word for mist wraps round the abbreviation for road

parts.note: steam is a kind of vapour or mist

explanation.surface: A fresh morning fog covers a road through a village.
explanation.definitionFit: This Dutch colony on Manhattan, later renamed New York, was a colonial settlement.

clue.text: Accommodating people from Usk initially trapped in 21

indicators.note: the three initials are caught inside the word that 21 gives

parts.note: 21 across is INFERNO, which here stands for its synonym hell

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Obliging folk from the Welsh town of Usk at first caught in a fiery hell.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference gives a synonym of 21's answer, not the answer itself. Usk is a small town in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: An accommodating person goes out of their way to assist, so is obliging and of use.

clue.text: Turned up Bible edition that is wide in scope

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word up reads backwards

parts.note: RV is the Revised Version of the Bible
IE, id est, means that is
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A newly found edition of the Bible, broad in its range.
explanation.definitionFit: One's purview is the range of one's authority or concern, i.e. its scope.

clue.text: Issue tender where an indefinite number held in New York

indicators.note: the article and the number letter are held inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: N is the mathematician's indefinite number

explanation.surface: Putting out a tender bid where an unknown count is held in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue tender' reads as a business instruction; issue means children and the tender is the one who tends them.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny is employed to look after children, a carer of someone's offspring or issue.

clue.text: Places to broadcast mass medium production

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these two words' letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Places that air a mass-media production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' suggests broadcasting media; it is a spiritualist medium.
explanation.definitionFit: Ectoplasm is the substance a spiritualist is said to exude during a seance, so what a psychic produces.

clue.text: Put striker through paces in longer game?

definitions.meaning: read as a verb phrase: test a match, a striker being a match that is struck
international cricket lasting up to five days

explanation.surface: Coach puts a footballer through drills ready for a long game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' looks like a footballer; it is a match, so testing one is 'test match'. A Test match is international cricket played over up to five days.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's Test format lasts several days, far longer than other games, as the question mark hints.

clue.text: Author to wait on female relatives might you say?

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is said aloud to give the name

parts.note: to wait on is to serve, and aunts are female relatives

explanation.surface: A writer attends to his aunts, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Miguel de Cervantes wrote Don Quixote, making him one of Spain's greatest writers.

clue.text: Change direction having run through official legislation

indicators.note: the letter for run passes through, between, the official and the legislation

parts.note: a ref, referee, is a match official
an act is a piece of legislation
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An official changes course after a law is rushed through.
explanation.definitionFit: To refract is to bend light or sound as it passes into a new medium, altering its path.

clue.text: High-flyer communicates with it

parts.note: airs means voices or makes known, communicates
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A high achiever stays in touch with what's cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flyer' sounds like an ambitious person; it is literally something that flies high.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirigible balloon cruises through the sky, so it literally flies high.

clue.text: Thick? Way beyond stupid, on reflection!

indicators.note: beyond puts the abbreviation for way after the rest
reflection is a mirror image, so the word for stupid reads backwards

parts.note: dim means stupid
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Thick? Far past stupid, when you think about it!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick' looks like a synonym of stupid, but it is a noun: the thick of things.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the thick of something is to be in its very centre, so thick is a noun for the middle.

clue.text: Trotter, wild, should go to the gallows in Bow?

parts.note: must means should, ought to

indicators.note: Bow is in London's East End, where Cockney speech drops the H

parts.note: to be hanged is to go to the gallows, so hang

explanation.surface: Del Boy Trotter, a wild one, deserves the noose in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Trotter nods to Del Boy of the BBC sitcom Only Fools and Horses, but it means a horse; Bow is a Cockney district of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: The mustang is a feral horse of the American plains, a wild animal that trots.

clue.text: Police officers fail to notice fire

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
to miss something is to fail to notice it

explanation.surface: Detectives overlook an arson blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone is to sack them from their job, just as an employer may dismiss them.

clue.text: Fail to draw positive conclusion from Dante's work?

definitions.text: Fail to draw positive conclusion from
definitions.meaning: deduce the negative instead of a positive verdict
the first part of the Divine Comedy, the tour of hell

explanation.surface: Struggling to reach an upbeat verdict from the Divine Comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer as 'infer no': to deduce the negative rather than the positive.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferno is the first part of Dante's Divine Comedy, depicting hell; the question mark flags a part, not the whole work.

clue.text: Ancient line discovered in ordinary study

indicators.note: the line letter is found inside the ordinary and study pieces

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: An old verse turned up in a routine piece of research.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is an archaic adjective for times long past, as in 'the olden days'.

clue.text: Someone cruel near person taking us in

indicators.note: the stingy person is taking the pronoun into itself
in completes taking in, saying the pronoun goes inside

parts.note: near means stingy, so a near person is a skinflint

explanation.surface: A cruel figure close to someone who takes us in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' looks like close by, but it is the old sense mean or stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: A misuser abuses or ill-treats, so the word describes a person who is cruel to others.

clue.text: Hidden area in stone outbuilding

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight
a shed is an outbuilding

explanation.surface: A secret space in a stone garden hut.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Stashed means tucked away somewhere secret, so concealed from view.

clue.text: Worker sent round takes in dress for Hindu empress

indicators.note: the reversed worker takes the garment inside it
sent round means turned about, so the worker's letters run backwards

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect
a sari is the wrapped garment worn by Hindu women

explanation.surface: A worker sent around fits a Hindu empress's dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hindu empress' seems one phrase, but Hindu belongs to the dress, and empress alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a Russian tsar, an empress.

clue.text: Hurry, then stop, ordered retired pundit

indicators.note: ordered means arranged anew, so the letters of these two words are reshuffled
retired means withdrawn, going back, so the pundit's letters run backwards

parts.note: a sage is a learned person, like a pundit

explanation.surface: Speed up, then halt, a retired expert was told.
explanation.definitionFit: To press the accelerator pedal is an idiom for going faster, i.e. to hurry.
